# Project Nyx — Backlog

A running list of items intentionally deferred from the current build sequence. This is the destination for anything that would otherwise be said as "let's log that for the future."

**Access:** PM can type `view backlog`, `show backlog`, or any natural-language equivalent in a session — Claude reads this file and presents it grouped by priority, surfacing anything that blocks the current build phase first.

**Adding items:** Claude adds rows here proactively — do not wait for PM. When raising a "for the future" item mid-session, write it here before continuing. Include a one-line _why_ so future-you can re-evaluate without re-deriving the context.

**IDs:** sequential `B-NNN`. Never reuse. When closing an item, leave the row and mark `Status: Done — <session date>` rather than deleting.

**Priority:**
- **Now** — should be tackled in the current or next session; here only because it's outside the in-flight chunk
- **Next** — tackle within the next 2–3 sessions or the next build phase
- **Later** — real but not time-sensitive; revisit when conditions change (e.g. pre-prod, multi-pet, paid tier)

**Status — lead with a structured head.** The Status cell must **begin** with one state token from this fixed set, then the date and resolving PR, so the column reads true at a glance and drift is machine-checkable:

- `Open` — not started.
- `In progress — <date> (PR #N)` — actively being built; say what's left.
- `Partial — <date> (PR #N)` — a defined slice shipped, more deferred; name the remaining slices.
- `Blocked — <reason>` — can't proceed; state the blocker (usually an Open Question).
- `Done — <date> (PR #N)` — shipped. Keep the row (don't delete); never close without a resolving PR/session reference.

**Rewrite the head when state changes — do NOT append the update to the tail of an already-long cell.** The recurring drift this file suffers is exactly that: a row that *opens* with `draft PR #106` / `R1 slice scoped` while a `Done` marker sits buried 200 words later — so the column lies even though the truth is technically "in the row" (caught reactively as B-022/B-045 on 2026-05-31, B-040/B-051/B-075 on 2026-06-11). Narrative and history may stay **below** the head, but the first token must be current. `/wrap` Step 4 reconciles these rows for every B-ID a session touches; the `backlog-groomer` skill enforces the head.

Fine for the vomit case (colour/texture/foreign material at arm's length); **marginal-to-useless for 6pt ingredient text**, which is the case the row was originally filed for. Raising the cap is a separate decision with storage/vision-cost/upload-time consequences. Do the gesture work once, with **B-037** (swipe-down-to-dismiss + the tap affordance) — and note the two live gesture conflicts in the existing viewer: pinch inside a horizontal paging `ScrollView`, and single-tap-anywhere-to-dismiss vs. double-tap-to-zoom. | B-105 | Replace-photo path leaves a duplicate `event_attachments` row (+ orphan Storage object + orphan local file) | Replacing a photo (event detail or edit-event add-over) INSERTs a NEW `event_attachments` row without removing the prior one, so a replaced event has ≥2 rows; `getEventAttachment`'s `ORDER BY sort_order LIMIT 1` (all `sort_order=0`) is rowid-ambiguous (the replace can appear not to take), and the prior Storage object + (post-B-104) doc-dir file orphan. **Pre-existing.** Fix: before inserting a replacement, soft-remove the prior (DB row + file + best-effort Storage `.remove`), or enforce one-attachment-per-event. | Next | 2026-06-16 | — | **Done — 2026-07-29 (PR #512).** Both halves shipped, and the diagnosis was confirmed against live data first: **3 events already carry duplicate rows in production** (all `vomit`, one pet, the second row landing 1–3 days after the first — the replace signature exactly), every row `sort_order = 0`. **Write half:** `lib/attachments.ts` is now the single implementation of "detach a photo" — local row + on-device file (awaited, throws), then best-effort Storage `.remove` and remote row delete (never throws; cleanup must work offline). The event-detail **Remove photo** handler, which already had this logic correct, was refactored onto it rather than the logic being written a second time. Both replace paths (`app/event/[id].tsx launchPicker`, `app/edit-event.tsx`) now sweep their priors through it. Two orderings are load-bearing and commented as such: the sweep runs **after** the replacement row is inserted *and* its upload is in flight (deleting first would turn a failed insert into an event with **no** photo — a worse bug than a duplicate; sweeping before the upload would put a Storage round-trip in front of the owner's new photo), and Storage is removed **before** the remote row (a crash between leaves a row naming a missing object, which renders the empty state, rather than bytes no row names — which the sign-out wipe walks `local_uri` to find and therefore cannot see). The sweep takes the **whole** prior list rather than the row the screen had loaded, so an already-duplicated event heals on its next replace. **Read half:** the queries moved to an I/O-free `lib/eventAttachmentQueries.ts` (the `foodQueries.ts` precedent) and order `sort_order ASC, created_at DESC, id DESC`. That is not cosmetic — it is what makes the write half safe in the two windows the client cannot close: `hydrateEventAttachments` is **insert-if-absent**, so a remote row surviving a failed delete is re-inserted on the next pull, and an upload already in flight when its row was replaced can `upsert` after the delete. Both are always **older** than the row that replaced them, so neither can win the read. Being a read fix, it also repairs already-duplicated installs **on sight**, with no replace and no migration. 19 new tests: the ordering runs for real against `node:sqlite` built from the production DDL (a string assertion could not have caught this — `ORDER BY sort_order ASC LIMIT 1` *looks* deterministic), including a regression test that demonstrates the old query returning **the replaced photo** when insertion order is reversed, and an all-permutations check that the answer is a function of the data rather than of insertion order. **Not retroactive on the server:** the 3 live duplicate rows still render two photo cards per incident in the vet report (`report.ts` renders *every* attachment per incident, deterministically sorted — so no ambiguity there, just doubling). Cleaning them is a live destructive write on health photos → PM action item, not taken here. Shipped via #512. |

| B-138 | Medication-confounder (PR 9) calibration residuals — dose-point under-detection + incidental-drug over-suppression | Surfaced by the adversarial-reviewer on B-117 PR 9. Two ACCEPTED, safe-direction limitations of the §8 confounder pass — both logged for Data-Scientist/Dr. Chen calibration, neither a code bug, neither ever falsely reassures (the cardinal invariant held): **(a) dose-as-point under-detection** — an administered dose is modeled as a POINT in `[onset−W, onset]` (like a meal), so a once-daily LONG-ACTING, regimen-UNLINKED drug dosed > W hours before onset (e.g. 06:00 dose, 21:00 vomit, 12h vomit window) is invisible → the confounder isn't caught → a false food correlation can surface (UNDER-suppression). Safe direction (never reassurance; degrades to today's no-med behavior). Robust fix = the regimen SPAN, which only exists once a regimen is set up (doses are regimen-unlinked today, B-135); a dose-persistence/tail is the alternative but reintroduces an arbitrary window — a Dr. Chen window-shape call (composes with the B-135 revisit). **(b) incidental-drug over-suppression** — mirroring the free-fed standing cap, a single incidental/PRN dose in any matched window caps the finding at Early; reviewer Monte-Carlo (real beef→vomit pet + ~5 random PRN doses/40d) wrongly SUPPRESSES the real finding ~4.8% and caps it at Early ~55%. Conservative by design, but it bounds how often the pass nicks a real correlation for PRN/chronically-medicated pets (the diet-trial wedge). Decision for Data-Scientist/PM: tune (require a dose persistence/tail; or cap-not-suppress below a dose-count floor) or ratify as the conservative v1. NOTE: the higher-severity Bonferroni family-shrink tier-inflation the same review found was FIXED in PR 9 (`suppressedFamilyCount` keeps withdrawn candidates in the family + regression test), not deferred here. | Later | 2026-06-20 | Step 10 / B-117 PR 9 follow-up | Open — calibration, carries a Data-Scientist/PM call |

The rule: assert only what the owner asserted, ask whenever the record is open — in-doubt keeps "Did {pet} still get it?", an unset dose keeps "Did {pet} take it?", **and so does a combo whose vehicle isn't rated yet** (`isGivenAssumed`). That last branch was the adversarial-review catch and it is the CANONICAL flow, not an edge: the intake chips and "+ Add a med given with this" share the meal card, so a pill-in-food combo is logged at serving time with `intake_rating` null → `initialComboDoseAdherence` returns `'given'` as an app default under uncertainty. Restating that as "Pixel took it" would assert *consumption* from an *administration* — the exact asymmetry PR B3 exists to protect — so it keeps the question. Safe because the line is an echo of the owner's own tap, not an app-generated claim: it asserts nothing the lit chip doesn't and changes no default. In a western tz (e.g. UTC-10), a full meal logged local-evening of the window's end day has a UTC instant *after* that boundary → negative gap → `Math.max(0,…)` floors it to `0 h`. | B-267 | iOS camera + photo-library permission usage strings missing from `app.json` | `expo-image-picker` drives camera (`requestCameraPermissionsAsync`/`launchCameraAsync`) and library (`requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync`) across food-capture, medication-capture, incident photos, and pet photos, but `app.json` sets no `NSCameraUsageDescription`/`NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` (only `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`) and does **not** list the `expo-image-picker` config plugin in `plugins` — so no purpose strings are injected at prebuild. iOS **crashes** an app that requests a permission with no purpose string, and App Review rejects a missing/blank one (Guideline 5.1.1). Fix: add `expo-image-picker` to `plugins` with explicit `cameraPermission`/`photosPermission`/`microphonePermission` copy (the plugin sets all three — camera capture can include video; Nyx-voice, states *why* — "so you can add a photo of a meal, symptom, or medication label"; Apple rejects generic "needs camera access" strings), verify the prebuilt Info.plist carries all keys. | B-443 | Ask's trial day counter is only as good as `user_profiles.timezone`, which defaults to New York | B-421 made `ask/tools.ts dietTrialStatus` bucket by the owner's stored zone — correct when the zone is correct. Two gaps remain, and the reachable one is not the one the code guards. **(a)** The fallback asymmetry: the client's fallback is the DEVICE zone, the server's is UTC, so a Sydney owner with no stored zone sees card **Day 5** / Ask **Day 4**. **(b)** The reachable case: `timezone` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'America/New_York'` (migration 001), so a profile whose `stampTimezone` never ran never *reaches* the fallback — it buckets a Kolkata owner's day by New York and disagrees with the card for ~10.5h of every day, with nothing in the code aware anything is wrong. | B-434 | `deno.lock` workspace block is stale (pre-SDK-57), so CI can't use `--frozen` | Found building B-390 (PR #440). `deno.lock`'s `workspace.dependencies` still mirrors the **pre-SDK-57** `package.json` (`expo@~54.0.35`, `jest-expo@54.0`, `babel-preset-expo@~54.0.10`, `@types/react@19.1`, …), so Deno rewrites the lockfile on every invocation and `deno cache --frozen` **fails on a clean checkout** (reproduced). CI therefore runs plain `--lock=deno.lock` — which still verifies every remote file against its committed hash (the part with security value: a `deno.land`/`esm.sh` URL whose content silently changed fails the build) but cannot catch lockfile drift. Note a bare regenerate does **not** stick: the next `package.json` bump re-staleifies the block, and `--frozen` would then red every dependency PR until someone remembered to re-run Deno. So the fix wants to be self-enforcing — either (a) regenerate + a CI step that fails if `deno.lock` is dirty after the run, or (b) stop tracking the npm workspace in `deno.lock` at all, since the Edge Functions never import `npm:` specifiers from `package.json`. Decide before turning `--frozen` on. | Later | 2026-07-25 | CI `--frozen` posture (B-390) | Open — filed 2026-07-25 (PR #440); plain `--lock` integrity checking is the interim mitigation. |

The CLI compares local file versions against that column, so **not one** of those 26 files is recognised as applied; the backfill only fixed the 18 it recorded (matched files 0/44 → 18/44). A bare `supabase db push` would still try to re-run 26 migrations — several with bare `CREATE TYPE` / `CREATE TABLE` / `ADD COLUMN` that error or partially apply, and some (e.g. `006`, were it in that set) would *re-open* RLS holes later migrations closed. Every new `apply_migration` adds one more mismatch (a sibling's `vet_documents` did exactly that mid-session). Options for the PM/Eng: **(a)** `UPDATE` the 26 rows' `version` to the filename prefix — one row per change, keeps `created_by`, loses the applied-at timestamp encoded in `version`; **(b)** add a *second* row per file keyed on the prefix — safe for `db push` but duplicates history; **(c)** rename the 26 files to their recorded timestamps — breaks the `NNN` convention that docs, PRs and CLAUDE.md reference everywhere; **(d)** accept it — the documented deploy path is the MCP, not `db push`, so treat history as documentation/drift-detection only and never run `db push`. (d) is the status quo and is defensible; it just needs to be a *decision* rather than an accident, and if chosen, `db push` should be explicitly warned against in the deploy runbook. | Later | 2026-07-26 | Any future `supabase db push` / CLI-from-disk flow; B-506 | Open |

| B-254 | Bind `vet_reports` INSERT `pet_id` + `storage_path` to the owner (defense-in-depth for the public link) | `rls-privacy-reviewer` on PR 6: `vet_reports_owner` (`FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = generated_by)`) gates only `generated_by` on INSERT — a user can `POST /rest/v1/vet_reports` directly with `generated_by = self`, an arbitrary `pet_id`, and an **attacker-chosen `storage_path`**, then read back their own row's default `share_token` and drive `view-report` to `download()` that key from `nyx-vet-reports`. **Not exploitable today**: the bucket is hardcoded (no cross-bucket traversal), keys are two server-generated UUIDv4s (~244 bits — a victim's report key is unguessable), and `view-report` only ever downloads a *named* key (never lists). So it's "safe by entropy," not "safe by construction." Fix (own schema/RLS PR + `rls-privacy-reviewer`, mirroring B-244): a `WITH CHECK` / `BEFORE INSERT` binding `pet_id IN (SELECT id FROM pets WHERE user_id = auth.uid())` **and** `storage_path LIKE pet_id || '/%'`. Turns the crafted-path insert impossible by construction. Two traps found by reading `app/_layout.tsx` against the Supabase flow and now load-bearing in the spec: (1) a recovery session is adopted unconditionally by the root listener, landing the owner on Home with their password still unknown → the FR-6 recovery gate; (2) a recovery link for account B tapped on a device signed in as A swaps the session while local SQLite + the App Group + the **widget timeline on the Home Screen** still hold A's pet data → the FR-7 `wipeLocalSession()` ordering. Elevated Next→Now by the 2026-07-20 hardening audit §B2. **Three gates ran on v1.0 (spec §12): `nyx-voice` ✓, `pm-feature-review` 2 SHIP-SHAPED / 2 NEEDS-WORK / 1 INSUFFICIENT, and `rls-privacy-reviewer` **FAIL with 5 merge blockers** — all folded into v1.1.** The blockers shared one root cause worth carrying forward: `wipeLocalSession()` was written for the `SIGNED_OUT` transition (session → **null**), but a recovery swap is non-null → non-null, so the session-keyed producers (`useWidgetSnapshots`, `useSync`) **re-arm instead of unmounting** and re-publish the previous owner's pets to the App Group + Home Screen widget *after* the wipe. §6.4 now forces a real `signOut()` before the exchange and reuses the shipped teardown. Also fixed: the gate must be **persisted** (in-memory died on force-quit while the recovery session persisted), cleared in a `finally` (a failed exchange wedged the app), gated on **local provenance** (`nyx:///reset-password?code=x` is firable by any app), and given a **router enforcement point** (none exists — widget deep links walked past it). Answer (spec §7.1): App Review has **no** guideline here and cannot test it, so it is a product/security call, not a compliance one; but the **standard control is to terminate other sessions on reset**, and the original "no" recommendation never checked it. **Team recommendation therefore CHANGED to "yes on reset (default), optional on change"** — a reset that evicts nothing leaves an attacker's refresh token renewing indefinitely while the owner believes they fixed it. Two conditions attach: the evicted device needs a designed "you were signed out because your password changed" state (reusing the B-039 one-shot banner), and the password-changed notification email must be on. |

For a witnessed event logged live (`occurred_at ≈ now`) they coincide, but for a **back-dated / discovered** event (`occurred_at` well before `now`) the SQL floor can drop a prior in-window event that `within()` would have counted → `repeated_loose_stool` / `repeated_vomiting` under-fires. `concurrent_vomiting`/`concurrent_lethargy` have the same now-vs-event anchor. Under-escalation only (never a false escalation, never a false reassurance), bounded to retroactively-dated events; **inherited from shipped vomit, not introduced by PR 3.** Fix consistently in both functions: anchor the fetch window to `thisEventOccurredAt` (widen the SQL floor to `occurred_at - windowHours`), or fetch a wider band and let `within()` do the gating. A stray hyphen is not a judgement call, and the merge risk was empirically **zero** (0 of 59 live rows), so the change is behaviour-neutral today and strictly correct going forward. Now **D3a** (spec §10): Class A (orthographic/artifact) merges are permitted on read, retroactively; Class B (semantic) stays write-path-only. | B-494 | A cat refusing nearly every meal of a prescribed diet raises NO safety flag on the vet report | **Found by the `vet-report-cold-read` on B-417 PR 7, and it is the most serious finding of that pass.** The rendered artifact holds an 8-year-old cat with **34 of 38 feedings of the trial diet logged as refused across 19 days**, **&minus;0.3 kg on a 4.4 kg body (~6.8% of body weight in 18 days)**, active chronic vomiting, and a free-fed bowl whose intake is by definition unobserved — the canonical feline anorexia / hepatic-lipidosis picture — and `snapshot.safetyFlags` is **empty**, so the report renders **no safety band at all**. The quieter-looking of the two artifacts is the sicker patient. Root cause is known and documented, not mysterious: `detectIntakeDecline` is a RELATIVE-decline detector, so a diet refused from day 1 is uniformly low rather than declining and returns `{status:'none'}` — PR 5's `trialDietRefusal` exists precisely because of this and is rendered on the card and in the trial block, but it is **not a `SafetyFlag`**, so it never reaches the band. Fix direction: either a trial-refusal safety lane keyed on PR 5's already-tuned floors (`REFUSAL_MIN_RATED`/`MIN_DAYS`/`SHARE`), or extend the intake detector to fire on a sustained ABSOLUTE floor rather than a relative fall. **Deliberately not done in PR 7** — a new clinical escalation path is load-bearing and needs the `adversarial-reviewer` pass + Dr. Chen that the DoD requires, and PR 7's mandated gate was the cold read. `clinical-guardrails` applies; intake is not preference. **Two cold reads disagree on whether this blocks the report, and the disagreement is not resolved:** round 3's Dr. Chen **withdrew it as a blocker** once page 1 composed the refusal with the weight delta as % of body weight; round 4's Dr. Chen — a fresh context, given the same artifact — ranked it **blocking #1**, on the ground that the report *teaches* the reader to scan the flag zone (*"Safety flags — Shown only when present, above the fold"*) and the honest legend disclaiming it sits on the last page, so composition mid-page does not repair the 60-second scan. Their words: *"the quieter-looking of the two artifacts is the sicker patient."* **RULED 2026-07-26 — the PM delegated the call to the product team, and the team ruled it BLOCKING FOR THE DEPLOY, not for the merge.** Rationale, and the conflict resolved rather than split: Dr. Chen carries this lens and two of three independent cold reads called it blocking, with a mechanism neither the Designer's nor Jordan's counter-lens rebuts — the report *teaches* the reader to scan the flag zone, and the legend then states affirmatively that no reduced-intake flag fired, so an empty band is read as a negative result rather than as silence. That is reassurance-on-absence at the report layer, which `clinical-guardrails` forbids outright, and *intake is not preference* routes refusal toward a health flag by invariant. The usual counter-argument — alarm fatigue, don't cry wolf — does not apply here: 38-of-38 refusals with ~7% body-weight loss in an 8-year-old cat with active chronic vomiting is not a marginal detector firing, it is the canonical case. **So: B-417 PR 7 merges (its own trial block is correct and regression-tested), `generate-report` is NOT redeployed until this lane exists,** and the artifact an owner can generate keeps the pre-PR-7 behaviour in the meantime. B-479 is therefore the gate on the redeploy, and it still needs its own `adversarial-reviewer` pass + Dr. Chen sign-off per the DoD — this ruling sets the bar, it does not waive the gates. | Now | 2026-07-26 | **Gates the `generate-report` redeploy** (B-417 PR 7 is merged but deliberately not deployed) | **Done — 2026-07-28 (PR #503).** The refused prescribed diet reaches the safety band: new `SafetyFlag` kind `trial_diet_refusal`, built in `report.ts` from the trial block's `rangeRefusal ?? trialDietRefusal` (the RANGE fact — a report is a history, and the 14-day recency bound would drop the flag on a cat whose ratings went quiet) or from an owner-declared `stopped_reason='refused'` with no counts invented. Rendered by `safetyFlagRow`, ordered with the intake family, and COMPOSED with the trial-scoped weight delta on the flag itself — the cold read's finding was that every fact was already on the page and never put together. Presence-only, never suppressed by `intake_decline` (different findings over different populations), and the legend now names the lane so the zone it teaches the reader to scan matches what actually watches it. Reaches the refusing cat even when food identity misses, via B-530's fallback. **Still gated on the fresh `vet-report-cold-read` before the `generate-report` redeploy**, per the Bucket-A plan. |

Mutation-validated four ways (drop `SECURITY DEFINER` on replace; re-grant anon; revoke `record_ai_usage`'s load-bearing grant; unpin `search_path`) — each turns the suite red. Advisory-lock TOCTOU: NOT revisited, still 045's shape. |

The recovery spec's §6.4 orders the handler **step 5 `supabase.auth.signOut()` → step 6 `exchangeCodeForSession(code)`** — deliberately, and for a good reason: forcing the session to null first means the shipped, tested `SIGNED_OUT` teardown runs instead of a second one written for a non-null → non-null swap (the fix for `rls-privacy-reviewer`'s five blockers). But as written, step 5 deletes the credential step 6 needs, so **every** recovery exchange would fail — and fail as `wrong_device`, since `classifyExchangeOutcome` maps auth-js's *"both auth code and code verifier should be non-empty"* to exactly that. The owner would be told to open the link on the phone they are already holding. Note this is invisible to a unit test: `passwordRecovery.ts` is pure and its 39 cases all pass. It surfaces only against the real client, which is why it is filed rather than left to §9.3's device checks to discover. Options for PR 2: **(a)** read the verifier before the sign-out and restore it after (works, but writes into auth-js's private storage key — fragile across upgrades); **(b)** exchange first, then run the teardown, accepting the swap window §6.4 was written to close; **(c)** re-sequence so the wipe happens without `signOut()` — i.e. the second teardown §6.4 was avoiding. None is free; the choice belongs with the §6.4 author. B-432's confirm handler does **not** need to pick one: it declines to exchange while a session is live, which recovery cannot copy because there the exchange *is* the flow. **RESOLVED IN SPEC v1.3 (2026-08-01): option (d), plus a fourth option the row hadn't filed.** §6.4 now nulls the *store* session (`setSession(null)` + `wipeLocalSession()`) instead of calling `supabase.auth.signOut()` — the producers (`useSync.ts:13`, `useWidgetSnapshots.ts:30`) key on `useAuthStore`, **not** on the client, so the store-null transition stands them down exactly as `SIGNED_OUT` does while leaving the verifier intact. `signOut()` was §6.4's *mechanism* (reach the null so the shipped teardown runs), never its *requirement*; nulling the store reaches the same teardown without touching the verifier — so this is not option (a)'s private-key surgery, not (b)'s reopened swap window, and not (c)'s "second teardown" (it *is* `wipeLocalSession()`, called directly). The one hazard it introduces — a nulled store while auth-js still holds the previous owner's tokens, which `autoRefresh` could silently restore onto the just-wiped device — is closed by a real `signOut()` on the failure path (FR-15's `finally`), safe there because the exchange has already failed and no live PKCE flow remains. The concurrent one: a trial is often a wet AND a dry of the same diet (&sect;4.1), so re-shooting only the dry keeps the narrow population non-empty in every window, and a cat eating the wet while refusing the dry reads as eating. Emptiness cannot see that, and a share test would fire on every legitimate mixed record. **(2) Dilution.** The wide population is a SHARE over every non-treat feeding, so a substitute the pet DOES eat sits in the denominator — executed: 14 of 14 prescribed bowls refused across 14 days plus 28 finished tuna meals dilutes below `REFUSAL_SHARE` and the lane goes quiet, where the identical record with intact identity fires. The narrow population is immune by construction (tuna is not `primary_diet`), so *&ldquo;the same floors over the meal record&rdquo;* is **not** a like-for-like substitution — the floors mean something different over a mixed population, and the first cut's docstring disclosed only the survivable direction of that trade. The repair is a **DURATION** criterion rather than a share, which is a clinical number and already Dr. Chen's open call in **B-575**. _(Filed as **B-576** on the #503 branch; **renumbered to B-579** when that branch merged `main` — a sibling session had taken B-576 for the `signOut()` PKCE-verifier row that blocks B-280 PR 2, and B-577/B-578 for the `nyx-food-photos` rows. Full chain recorded per the B-505 wrap lesson: a note that records one hop sends the next reader to the wrong row.)_ | Now | 2026-07-28 | B-529 (identity); pairs B-575 | Open |

| B-699 | Divergent-key re-photo of the trial diet evades rung-1 dedup → over-fires both log-time flags on the prescribed diet | _(filed as B-694, **renumbered to B-699** at this wrap’s merge from `main` — B-694 was taken on `main` first by the med-history refusal-visibility row, #587; first-lands-keeps per B-435.)_ **Found by `adversarial-reviewer` on B-693 PR 1 (2026-08-04, findings P3 + P2). OVER-FIRE, not reassurance — not a ship blocker, but a real gap on the one food that must never alarm-fatigue.** The §5.4 duplicate-capture guard (`matchAllowed`, `lib/dietTrial.ts`) silences a re-photographed diet only when the new capture's `foodKey` EXACTLY equals the stored allowed-set key. Two captures of the same physical bag can extract divergent brand+product text (AI-extraction variance, or a manual "Duck" vs "Duck Formula") — `food_items_cache.brand`/`product_name` are `TEXT NOT NULL` so it is genuine text divergence, not partial hydration — so keys diverge, rung 1 misses on both id and key, and the feeding falls through: **membership** ("isn't on the trial list") on the duck-only re-photo, or **contents** ("this has chicken") when the re-photo's panel newly reads an off-trial protein, both on the PRESCRIBED diet (C2 alarm-fatigue inversion). Pre-existing for the contents flag; B-693 extended it to the previously-silent membership case. Bounded to once per uuid by the heads-up ledger, self-healed by the add-to-list escape hatch (one tap adds the new capture), and never the reassurance/silence direction — which is why it ships. Related lower-severity case (P2): a vet-permitted food added mid-trial on another device, logged before its `diet_trial_foods` row syncs, over-fires membership on this device (the guard checks only primary rows; the missing permitted row is undetectable — transient, TTL + sync). Fix is a shared dedup improvement in `matchAllowed` (fuzzy/normalized name match or a stable capture lineage id), which is **Deno-shared** (client + `generate-report` + `ask`) and cross-cutting, so out of any lib-only surface PR. Pinned red-test-ready by `lib/trialContaminant.test.ts` ("KNOWN over-fire (B-699)"). | Later | 2026-08-04 | — | Open |
